title: Unit – 5 : Session – 1 : SLO – 2  |  Types of Graphs
sections: I. Definitions
a) Simple Graph: an undirected graph with no self-loops and no multiple edges between the same pair of vertices.
b) Directed Graph (digraph): a graph in which every edge has a direction, going from one vertex to another.
c) Weighted Graph: a graph in which each edge carries a value (weight) such as cost, distance or time.
d) Complete Graph: a graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is connected by an edge (n(n-1)/2 edges).
e) Null Graph: a graph with vertices but no edges.
f) Connected Graph: a graph in which a path exists between every pair of vertices.
g) Disconnected Graph: a graph in which at least one pair of vertices has no path between them.
h) Multigraph: a graph that allows multiple (parallel) edges between the same pair of vertices.
i) Subgraph: a graph whose vertices and edges are subsets of another graph's vertices and edges.
j) Cyclic Graph: a graph that contains at least one cycle (a path that starts and ends at the same vertex).
k) Undirected Graph: a graph in which edges have no direction; edge (u, v) is the same as (v, u).
II. Diagrams for Three Graph Types
Simple graph:  A---B   (plain edges, no loops)
C---D
Directed graph: A -> B -> C -> A  (arrows show direction of edges)
Weighted graph: A --5-- B
C --4-- D   (numbers on edges are weights)
III. True or False
a) A complete graph with 'n' vertices has n(n-1)/2 edges — TRUE.
b) In a weighted graph, no values are assigned to edges — FALSE.
c) A directed graph has edges with direction — TRUE.
d) A multigraph allows multiple edges between two vertices — TRUE.
IV. Match the Following
a) Weighted Graph — ii) Values on edges
b) Null Graph — i) No edges
c) Directed Graph — iv) Arrows showing direction
d) Multigraph — iii) Loops or multiple edges
V. Real-Life Applications
Weighted graph: road networks in Google Maps (edge weight = distance/travel time) for shortest-path routing.
Directed graph: Twitter/Instagram 'follow' relationships (one-way edges), or web links between pages.
Complete graph: round-robin tournament scheduling where every team plays every other team.
Null graph: a set of newly added users in a network with no connections yet.
